Greene Criticizes Trump’s ‘Super Intelligence’ Rebrand
Greene made the comments Friday on
X
while sharing a
Truth Social
post from Trump following his meeting with Chinese President
Xi Jinping
Trump said Xi appeared to support replacing the term "Artificial Intelligence" with "SUPER INTELLIGENCE," calling the new name "more accurate and important."

Greene dismissed the terminology change, writing, "Changing the name Artificial Intelligence to ‘Super’ Intelligence" would not suddenly make Americans support building data centers in their communities.
She specifically pointed to data centers’ water consumption and "24/7 noise," highlighting concerns over the environmental and community impacts of the infrastructure needed to support the AI boom.

children: AI Data Centers Face Growing Resource Concerns
The debate comes as AI companies accelerate data center construction across the U.S. to meet rising computing demand.
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
directly consumed about 66 billion liters of water in 2023, up from 21.2 billion liters in 2014.
Hyperscale facilities could consume between 60 billion and 124 billion liters annually by 2028.

However, water consumption varies significantly by facility and cooling technology. The Data Center Coalition says some facilities use air cooling, while others rely on water-based or hybrid systems. Operators are also deploying closed-loop and waterless cooling technologies.
